title: FrameDesk — studio approvals app and API
brief: Review example 2 of 2: a fictional multi-workspace app for studios to review assets and record approvals. Covers software, data, identity and operations nodes. Optional infrastructure is labeled explicitly.
objective: Let a studio share a protected asset, collect an authorized approval and recover safely from expired sessions or failed processing.
success: A reviewer can explain the main path and identify the unresolved choices.
Technology names, rationale and diagram nodes can be annotated individually.
No optional capability is silently treated as a launch requirement.

now: Explicit identity verification, membership checks and auditable approvals.
A small modular backend plus a browser client; optional scaling components remain deferred.
later: Only add optional capabilities after evidence supports them.
out: Purchasing services, deploying systems or producing final creative assets during this review.

context.detail: This is a fictional but concrete review plan created to exercise the planning toolkit and its node types.
context.source: User request: create two or three plans covering the node catalogue.

context.detail: Actual budget, team capacity, existing systems and delivery dates have not been supplied.
Technology and production-tool choices below are reviewable proposals, not approved purchases.

technologies.name: TypeScript
technologies.role: Shared language for browser and server modules.
technologies.rationale: Makes interfaces and refactors easier to check across the app.
technologies.tradeoffs: Type checking does not validate untrusted runtime input.
alternatives: Use the existing project language when an established codebase already exists.
impacts: Build tooling, types and package compatibility
checks: Choose compatible runtime/build versions and commit one lockfile.
technologies.versionPlan: No versions are fabricated or installed in this planning example. Before implementation, inspect existing manifests, choose compatible supported releases, record exact versions in the lockfile, and test updates.

technologies.name: Supabase Postgres
technologies.role: Authoritative workspace, membership, project and approval records.
technologies.rationale: A relational starting point for records that need explicit ownership and constraints.
technologies.tradeoffs: Tenant isolation, migrations, pooling and restore behavior require design and tests.
impacts: Data model, migrations, permissions and backups
checks: Test forbidden cross-workspace reads and writes.
Rehearse migration and restore with non-production data.
technologies.versionPlan: No versions are fabricated or installed in this planning example. Before implementation, inspect existing manifests, choose compatible supported releases, record exact versions in the lockfile, and test updates.

technologies.name: Supabase Auth
technologies.role: Managed sign-in, recovery and session identity.
technologies.rationale: Avoids a second home-built credential store while keeping application authorization explicit.
technologies.tradeoffs: Provider behavior, redirects, session expiry and offboarding must be verified.
alternatives: Evaluate another managed identity service if required enterprise features are missing.
impacts: Login, recovery, token verification, logout and workspace membership
checks: Test valid, expired, malformed and wrong-audience tokens.
Verify recovery, session expiry and removed-member access.
technologies.versionPlan: No versions are fabricated or installed in this planning example. Before implementation, inspect existing manifests, choose compatible supported releases, record exact versions in the lockfile, and test updates.

technologies.name: Node.js + Fastify
technologies.role: One modular HTTP API for assets, membership and approvals.
technologies.rationale: Keeps server responsibilities explicit and independently testable without splitting into microservices.
technologies.tradeoffs: A separately hosted API introduces deployment and contract coordination.
alternatives: A full-stack framework already used by the team.
impacts: HTTP contracts, authorization checks, validation and error handling
checks: Check workspace membership server-side on every protected operation.
technologies.versionPlan: No versions are fabricated or installed in this planning example. Before implementation, inspect existing manifests, choose compatible supported releases, record exact versions in the lockfile, and test updates.

technologies.name: React + Vite
technologies.role: Browser UI, review states and locally validated forms.
technologies.rationale: A proposed client stack for an interaction-heavy approval workflow.
technologies.tradeoffs: Client routing, fetching, accessible controls and loading/error states still need explicit choices.
alternatives: A server-rendered approach if the final experience is mostly content.
impacts: Routes, forms, components and session presentation
checks: Test keyboard review and recovery without losing notes.
Verify the production build and supported browsers.
technologies.versionPlan: No versions are fabricated or installed in this planning example. Before implementation, inspect existing manifests, choose compatible supported releases, record exact versions in the lockfile, and test updates.

technologies.name: Supabase Storage
technologies.role: Private asset files separate from relational metadata.
technologies.rationale: Fits a review workflow needing controlled file access.
technologies.tradeoffs: File policy, upload limits, retention and temporary access must be checked.
impacts: Uploads, previews, download access and deletion
checks: Reject unauthorized file access and unsupported uploads.
Test access expiry and deleted-member behavior.
technologies.versionPlan: No versions are fabricated or installed in this planning example. Before implementation, inspect existing manifests, choose compatible supported releases, record exact versions in the lockfile, and test updates.

technologies.name: Render web service + static client hosting
technologies.role: Proposed hosting for the Node API and built client.
technologies.rationale: A managed deployment option to evaluate against the team’s existing hosting.
technologies.tradeoffs: Region, operational cost, capacity and background-job support remain to be checked.
alternatives: Reuse existing hosting if it meets runtime and data-location requirements.
impacts: Build commands, secrets, health checks and rollback
checks: Deploy an isolated staging build and verify configuration.
Rehearse rollback without losing recorded approvals.
technologies.source: https://render.com/docs/deploy-node-express-app — general Node hosting example; validate the Fastify setup separately.
technologies.versionPlan: No versions are fabricated or installed in this planning example. Before implementation, inspect existing manifests, choose compatible supported releases, record exact versions in the lockfile, and test updates.

technologies.name: BullMQ + Redis — deferred option
technologies.role: Optional heavier background-processing queue; not required for the initial synchronous approval path.
technologies.rationale: Consider only if measured processing volume needs a separate worker system.
technologies.tradeoffs: Adds queue operations, connection management and duplicate/retry handling.
alternatives: Start with a bounded durable job/outbox record and existing worker capability.
impacts: Workers, queue semantics, retries and hosting cost
checks: Demonstrate a workload that justifies the dependency.
Test duplicate jobs, worker restart and failed-job recovery.
technologies.versionPlan: No versions are fabricated or installed in this planning example. Before implementation, inspect existing manifests, choose compatible supported releases, record exact versions in the lockfile, and test updates.

technologies.name: Type checks + Vitest + Playwright + axe-core
technologies.role: Targeted verification of contracts, authorization and user journeys.
technologies.rationale: Covers code and browser behavior while using the existing quality workflow where possible.
technologies.tradeoffs: Passing checks does not establish all security or product quality.
alternatives: Reuse the project’s established equivalent test tools.
impacts: CI, contract tests and release criteria
checks: Run sign-in, expired-session, approval and upload error journeys.

diagrams.title: How do sign-in and permissions work?
diagrams.description: Supabase Auth establishes identity. Fastify and the data/file policies enforce permitted access; these are separate responsibilities.

layers.title: Whole picture
layers.description: Supabase Auth establishes identity. Fastify and the data/file policies enforce permitted access; these are separate responsibilities.

nodes.detail: Proposed flow: email sign-in through the provider, SDK-managed session handling, verified API credentials and explicit expiry/recovery. Exact session persistence must be selected and tested before coding.
Enforce permitted actions server-side, including removed members and access to another workspace.
Combine operation permission with resource ownership. Direct data/storage access also needs correctly tested provider policies.
Keep privileged credentials in hosting configuration, rotate them and limit access. This plan contains no real secret values.
Validate requests and identity before entering privileged operations. Expired or invalid sessions return a recoverable sign-in path.

diagrams.title: How do we ship, observe and recover?
diagrams.description: No infrastructure is deployed by this plan. The release path needs a reproducible build, tested configuration and a recovery route.

layers.title: Whole picture
layers.description: No infrastructure is deployed by this plan. The release path needs a reproducible build, tested configuration and a recovery route.

nodes.detail: Use an isolated preview, then a deliberate release with configuration and migration checks.
Validate runtime, health checks and capacity in the selected region before committing.
Configure the actual origin, API access and transport settings; avoid assuming default networking is sufficient.
Track meaningful errors and failed work, with a clear staff response.
Correlate requests and jobs; avoid credentials or private asset contents in logs.
Test cross-workspace access, expired sessions, retries and stale asset versions.
Document application rollback separately from recovering data after a bad migration.
